parts.title: Part 1 · Enquiry about a weekend photography course

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Part 1. You will hear a man phoning an arts centre to ask about a photography course. First, you have some time to look at questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 1 to 5.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Good morning, Westbank Arts Centre. How can I help you?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Hi. I saw a poster about a weekend photography course, and I'd like some more information.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Of course. We run two weekend courses at the moment. Can I take your name first?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Yes, it's Daniel Hartley.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Is that H-A-R-T-L-Y?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Almost. There's an E before the Y. H-A-R-T-L-E-Y.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Thank you. Now, have you done any photography courses before?

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Not really. I've had a camera for a couple of years, but I mostly use the automatic setting.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Then the intermediate course might move a little fast for you. I'd suggest the one for beginners. It covers the basic controls and how to compose a picture.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: That sounds right.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The beginners' course used to run on Sundays, but we've moved it, because the museum next door is closed on Sundays and we use its gardens for the outdoor practice. So it's now on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Saturday is fine. What time does it start?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The doors open at nine, and it's a good idea to arrive then if you need help setting up your camera, but the session itself begins at a quarter past nine.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: OK, so nine fifteen.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: That's right. And it finishes at about four.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Where exactly do we meet? Is it here at the arts centre?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Not for this course. The group meets at the museum. The main entrance is often busy with school groups on Saturday mornings, so please go to the garden entrance at the back of the building. The tutor will be waiting there.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the conversation, you have some time to look at questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now listen and answer questions 6 to 10.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: And how much does the course cost?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The full price is ninety-five pounds, but for members of the arts centre it's eighty-five.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: I'm not a member yet. Is it worth joining?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Membership is twenty pounds a year, so you'd save ten pounds on this course alone, and you'd get discounts on our other courses too.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: I think I'll join today, then. So the course would be eighty-five.

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Exactly. That includes lunch at the museum café, and at the end of the day you'll receive a certificate. Some people use it for their college applications.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Great. Do I need to bring anything?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Your camera, obviously, with a spare battery if you have one. You don't need a tripod; we lend those. The thing people most often forget is a raincoat. A lot of the day is outside, whatever the weather.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: A raincoat. OK. And how many people are usually in a group?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: We used to take up to fifteen, but the tutor found that was too many to give everyone enough attention, so the limit is now twelve.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: That sounds better. One last question: is there parking near the museum?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: The museum's own car park is for staff only. There's a public car park on Bridge Street, about two minutes' walk away, and it's free on Saturdays.

lines.speaker: Caller
lines.text: Bridge Street. Perfect. Can I book a place now?

lines.speaker: Receptionist
lines.text: Certainly. I'll just need a few more details.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That is the end of Part 1. You now have half a minute to check your answers.

parts.title: Part 2 · Volunteer orientation at a nature reserve

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Part 2. You will hear a volunteer coordinator welcoming new volunteers to a nature reserve. First, you have some time to look at questions 11 to 14.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now listen carefully and answer questions 11 to 14.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Good morning, everyone, and welcome to Greenfield Nature Reserve. My name's Helen Price, and I coordinate our volunteers. Before you start, I'll explain how the reserve works and what you'll be doing.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: First, a little history. The reserve was created in 1987, when the old gravel pits here were allowed to flood. Visitors often assume the lakes are natural, but every one of them was dug by machines for gravel. Today they attract more than a hundred and forty species of birds, although the number that visit each winter changes a great deal with the weather further north.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Many of you have asked about the timetable. Volunteer days run from Tuesday to Saturday. We tried Sunday sessions last year, but so many families visit at the weekend that the paths were too crowded for practical work, so Sunday is now for visitors only.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: As for what to wear, the reserve provides gloves and tools, and each of you will be given a high-visibility vest, which you must wear whenever you're working near the road. Please bring your own boots, though. We used to keep a supply, but finding the right sizes was always a problem.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: The reserve also has some rules that may seem strict. Dogs are welcome on the main circular path, but not on the lake trails, because of nesting birds. And please ask visitors not to feed the ducks bread. It's bad for them, and it attracts rats. The visitor centre sells bags of grain instead, and the money goes to the reserve.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Before you hear the rest of the talk, you have some time to look at questions 15 to 20.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: Now listen and answer questions 15 to 20.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Now let me tell you about the different areas on your map and the work we'll be doing in each this season.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Starting from the visitor centre, the first area you come to is the Reed Beds. The reeds there need cutting back every autumn, and that's the main job this month. It's hard work, but very satisfying.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Next to them is Kingfisher Lake. There's nothing for volunteers to do there at the moment, because the birds are breeding, so we keep people well away.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: The Meadow is where we're running a wildflower survey. Volunteers count the plants in marked squares. No experience is necessary; we'll train you.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: In the Woodland, our priority is the paths. Tree roots and mud have made some sections dangerous, so we're laying new surfaces.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: The Hide, the wooden building overlooking the main lake, is used by birdwatchers. We need volunteers there at weekends to chat with visitors and help them identify the birds they see. We had planned to build a second hide this year, but that's been postponed.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Finally, the Orchard. Last year we planted thirty young apple trees there, and they need protecting from rabbits, so we'll be putting a fence around each one.

lines.speaker: Coordinator
lines.text: Right. If you'd like to collect your vests from the table by the door, we'll make a start.

lines.speaker: Narrator
lines.text: That is the end of Part 2. You now have half a minute to check your answers.
